newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close softer, pressured by dollar.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close softer, pressured by dollar.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed a little softer on Friday, pressured by a weaker currency as investors attempted to push the central bank into a second short-term interest rate increase this year.

"The front end traded weaker all day long on the back of a weaker dollar," said Rob Palombi, MMS International analyst. "The FX (foreign exchange) community is still intent on testing the Bank of Canada for another rate hike."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.05 to C$120.14 to yield 6.467 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 7/32 to yield 6.46 percent and the spread between the bonds narrowed to one basis point from three at Thursday's close.
"Losses extended to long-date bonds this afternoon amid talk of a large seller (out of the United States)," Palombi said.

Palombi added that the market was awaiting next week's slew of U.S. and Canadian economic data. The most closely watched Canadian figure would be real gross domestic product for May, I.D.E.A. analyst Harvinder Kalirai said.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond dipped C$0.18 to C$109.57 to yield 5.949 percent.
The U.S. 10-year bond fell 5/32 to yield 6.18 percent and the negative spread between the bonds widened to 23 basis points from 24 basis points at Thursday's close.
